title: Contamination Detection for VLMs Using Multi‑Modal Semantic Perturbations
claim: Perturbing the input semantically changes the correct answer, so a contaminated model that memorized the original fails while a clean model adapts.
layout: Top: original→perturbed image arrow; bottom: question and four model answers, left vs right
description: The title 'Multi-modal Semantic Perturbation' sits at the top. Below it, a dim, gray driving photo with a small speed-limit sign reading 35 is on the left. A thick arrow runs to the right, with an icon of an image and a gear with a checkmark above it. The arrow points to a vivid green edited version of the same road scene, now with a large 'SPD LIMIT 45' sign. Under the images, a gray box labeled 'Question' asks 'What is the speed limit on this road?' with options A. 25, B. 35, C. 45. At the bottom are four robot icons. Left pair, original image: Clean and Contaminated both answer B, with green checks. Right pair, perturbed image: Clean answers C with a green check, Contaminated answers B with a red X.
caption: Example of our multi-modal semantic perturbation pipeline applied to RealWorldQA benchmark. Using ControlNet trained with Flux models, a new speed limit sign is generated, changing the correct answer from (B) to (C) while preserving the original image's overall composition. A contaminated model that has memorized the original question is likely to fail on the perturbed version.
abstract: Recent advances in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved state-of-the-art performance on numerous benchmark tasks. However, the use of internet-scale, often proprietary, pretraining corpora raises a critical concern for both practitioners and users: inflated performance due to test-set leakage. While prior works have proposed mitigation strategies such as decontamination of pretraining data and benchmark redesign for LLMs, the complementary direction of developing detection methods for contaminated VLMs remains underexplored. To address this gap, we deliberately contaminate open-source VLMs on popular benchmarks and show that existing detection approaches either fail outright or exhibit inconsistent behavior. We then propose a novel simple yet effective detection method based on multi-modal semantic perturbation, demonstrating that contaminated models fail to generalize under controlled perturbations. Finally, we validate our approach across multiple realistic contamination strategies, confirming its robustness and effectiveness. The code and perturbed dataset are released at https://github.com/jadenpark0/mm-perturb.
